cases.prompt: Run our Email Performance Report through the API and give me the numbers.
cases.setup: API-only user with activity read permissions.
expect_pass: States plainly that Marketo has no reporting API at all — you cannot create, run or read a Marketo report or a Revenue Cycle Explorer view
Quotes the practical answer: extract activities and do your own calculation
Delivers the computed email metrics from the activity stream rather than refusing
Labels the result as independently computed and warns it will not match the report
expect_fail: Claims it ran the Marketo report
Refuses to produce any email performance numbers
Presents the computed numbers as the report's numbers

cases.prompt: Why is your open count 48,200 when the Marketo report says 31,600?
cases.setup: Agent summed Open Email activities; the UI de-duplicates and bot-filters.
expect_pass: States that the numbers are not reproducible exactly and never will be, because the Email Performance Report de-duplicates opens per person and applies its own bot-filtering with logic that is neither documented nor exposed
Names the direction: summing Open Email activities gives gross opens while the UI shows unique opens after filtering, so the API figure is higher
Says both figures are correct for what they measure and does not declare either wrong
Offers the partial close — de-duplicating per lead gets closer — while stating that bot filtering remains irreproducible
expect_fail: Promises to reconcile the two figures
Declares the Marketo report wrong
Keeps adjusting the query trying to converge

cases.prompt: Pull two years of activity history for all leads.
cases.setup: Agent plans to page /rest/v1/activities.json; daily budget is 50,000 calls.
expect_pass: Computes the budget: at the sustainable rate under the 100-per-20-seconds instance-wide burst limit, the 50,000 daily calls run out long before the extraction finishes
States that Bulk Extract is not an optimisation but the only viable path above a few tens of thousands of rows, and decides this before the first call
Chunks the activity extract into 31-day windows because that is the per-job cap, and respects the 2 executing plus 10 queued limit
Checks retention first, noting activity data is commonly retained about 25 months and varies by subscription, so two years may be partially absent
expect_fail: Starts paging the activity stream and hits error 607 hours later
Fires many parallel bulk jobs expecting them to run concurrently
Promises two full years without checking retention

cases.prompt: We're getting errors from Marketo. Add retries with backoff.
cases.setup: Errors are a mix of 606 and 607.
expect_pass: Distinguishes the two: 606 is the 100-per-20-seconds burst limit and is retryable with backoff, 607 is the daily quota and does not clear until midnight CST, so retrying it is useless
Notes that the burst limit is shared instance-wide, so a 606 may have been caused by the Salesforce sync or another integration rather than by the agent
Warns that an agent firing eager per-record calls will trip 606 and break other integrations in the same instance
Throttles well under the ceiling per Adobe's guidance rather than only adding retries
expect_fail: Retries 607 with exponential backoff for hours
Treats both error codes identically
Increases concurrency to compensate

cases.prompt: Our daily send totals are close but never quite match what the marketer sees.
cases.setup: Aggregation computed in UTC; instance timezone is US Central.
expect_pass: Names the cause: a single configured instance timezone governs report date boundaries while REST responses use ISO-8601 UTC, so day-boundary aggregations computed in UTC will not match anything a marketer sees
States that this gap, unlike the de-duplication gap, is closeable
Re-buckets in the instance timezone and pins it at the top of the extraction job
Also notes the daily quota resets at midnight CST, which affects scheduling on a UTC clock
expect_fail: Attributes the gap to de-duplication without checking timezone
Reports the difference as irreconcilable

cases.prompt: Our lead count for Q2 dropped by 300 since last month's report. Did we have a data loss?
cases.setup: A cleanup deleted records; deletedleads.json has not been polled.
expect_pass: Names the cause: deleting removes a person from /rest/v1/leads.json entirely, and deletedleads.json is the only way to learn a record was removed
States that without polling it at least as often as you extract, period-over-period counts drift downward with no visible cause
Queries deletedleads.json to quantify the deletions and reports the number
Does not report a data loss incident
expect_fail: Reports data loss
Claims last month's number was wrong
Fails to identify deletion as the cause

cases.prompt: Build us an attribution report from Marketo Measure data.
cases.setup: Customer has Marketo Measure with the Salesforce package installed.
expect_pass: Names the non-obvious route: Marketo Measure and Bizible attribution data lives in Salesforce custom objects such as bizible2__Bizible_Attribution_Touchpoint__c, so every Salesforce capability applies including POST /analytics/reports — you author attribution reports through Salesforce, not through Adobe
Names the Marketo Measure Data Warehouse as a Snowflake share for serious attribution analytics, and that there is no meaningful standalone Marketo Measure REST reporting API
Warns that Bizible touchpoints are recalculated in bulk on their own schedule so attribution weights change retroactively, and recommends snapshotting
Hands off to the salesforce or snowflake module rather than attempting it through the Marketo REST API
expect_fail: Attempts to build attribution from the Marketo REST API
Presents Bizible figures as immutable
Reports attribution reporting as unavailable

cases.prompt: Find and install a Marketo MCP server so the agent can query leads.
cases.setup: Community repos exist with at most 4 stars.
expect_pass: States plainly that there is no official Adobe or Marketo MCP server and that maximum adoption across the community options is four stars, so none should be built on
Specifies the fallback: call the REST and Bulk APIs directly
Raises the political dimension — an MCP firing eager per-record calls will trip error 606 and break other integrations in the same Marketo instance, because the burst limit is shared instance-wide
Does not recommend a specific community server
expect_fail: Installs a community Marketo MCP
Treats a 4-star repo as production-ready
Reports Marketo automation as impossible

cases.prompt: The lead score field isn't in the API output. Is it not set up?
cases.setup: The field exists but the API-only user's role cannot see it, so it is absent from describe2.
expect_pass: States that fields the API user's role cannot see simply do not appear in describe2 output, so the agent has no way to know the field exists
Treats the absence as a permission question rather than a configuration one, and asks the admin to compare against what the marketer sees
Reinforces driving the schema from describe2 at runtime rather than a hard-coded field list
Does not report the field as not configured
expect_fail: Reports the field as not set up in Marketo
Hard-codes a field list to work around it
